"Quack" as a noun carries two distinct meanings. One is simple and literal; the other is rich with social meaning and widely used in everyday conversation.
Meaning 1 — The sound a duck makes

A quack is the short, sharp, flat sound that comes out of a duck's mouth. It is the duck's natural call — the way a dog barks or a cat meows, a duck quacks. That individual sound is called "a quack."

Example: "Every time she tossed bread into the pond, she heard a chorus of quacks."

Simple as that. One quack, many quacks.
Meaning 2 — A fake doctor or medical fraud

This is the far more important and widely used meaning. A quack is a person who pretends to have medical knowledge or healing skills that they do not actually have. They lie about their expertise in order to deceive sick or desperate people — usually to take their money.

A quack might claim they can cure cancer, fix a broken spine, or reverse blindness — using a special herb, a magical device, a secret formula, or some invented therapy. None of it works, because none of it is real medicine. The quack knows this, but the patient does not.

The single most important thing to understand: A quack is not simply a bad doctor or an incompetent one. The defining feature is deliberate deception. An honest, well-meaning doctor who makes an error in diagnosis is not a quack. A person with no medical training whatsoever who hangs a fake certificate on the wall, calls themselves "Dr. Smith," and charges sick people money for worthless treatments — that is a quack.

Example: "After months of suffering, she desperately turned to a quack who promised to cure her with colored water and breathing exercises."

Example: "The government shut down the clinic after discovering the man running it was a quack with no medical degree."

Extended and looser use: While "quack" is strongest in the medical context, people sometimes use it more broadly to describe anyone who falsely poses as an expert in any serious professional field — a fake therapist, a fraudulent financial advisor, and so on. If someone is clearly unqualified yet confidently pretending to be an authority and profiting from that pretense, calling them a quack is understood. That said, the medical sense remains the core meaning, and when someone says "quack" without context, medicine is almost always what they mean.

The related word "quackery": The practice of being a quack — the whole system of fake cures, false claims, and medical fraud — is called quackery. This is a useful word to know alongside "quack."

Example: "The internet is unfortunately full of quackery, with people selling miracle supplements that have never been tested."

If you hear someone call a person a quack, they are saying: "Don't trust this person. They are pretending to know how to heal you, but they are a fraud." It is a word of warning and contempt — you use it to expose someone as a dangerous fake.

The duck sound meaning is entirely separate and context always makes it clear which meaning is intended. No one calling a duck a quack is insulting anyone.
